Subject: Elevated errors and slow inference since 03/14 - urgent

Hi Sofia / Ben,

We started seeing a sharp rise in inference errors and a sustained throughput drop across our checkout models starting ~14:30 UTC today. Error rate jumped from ~0.2% to 6%, and 95th p95 latency doubled. This is impacting checkout throughput for ~30% of live traffic.

Attached are the logs and a short excerpt from our metrics dashboard (pelican_logs_20280314.zip). Can you confirm receipt and an ETA for triage? We need an initial assessment and an expected time to mitigation; our execs are asking for an update within the hour.

Thanks,
Alex Torres
Head of Platform, Pelican Retail

We will post an interim update in 45 minutes.

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Torres <alex.torres@pelicanretail.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 09:45:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Elevated errors and slow inference since 03/14 - initial findings

Quick summary from our systems review so far (preliminary):
- Root symptom: a burst of requests with longer prefix lengths caused repeated KV cache misses which amplified decode cost and increased scheduling contention on the 8-GPU pool servicing Pelican.
- Contributing factor A: recent routing tweak (routed additional traffic to the larger model variant to avoid hallucinations) increased average token window and broke our optimistic cache hit assumptions.
- Contributing factor B: autoscaler hysteresis misconfiguration kept an older pod set pinned during the spike, delaying scale-up by ~4 minutes.

Immediate mitigations applied (15:10 UTC):
- Rolled back the routing tweak to the prior model variant for the checkout route.
- Applied temporary queue-weight cap to reduce head-of-line blocking.

Initial impact: error rate falling from 6% to ~1.5%, p95 latency trending down but still ~1.4x baseline.

Ben Carter
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Alex Torres <alex.torres@pelicanretail.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Mar 2028 13:20:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Elevated errors and slow inference since 03/14 - remediation plan and owners

Following the initial triage and Ben's findings, here's the remediation plan and owners. I've included timelines; this is intended for Pelican execs and our internal PM/infra leads.

Planned corrective actions:
1) KV cache sensitivity tuning and patch (owner: Karthik) — deliver patch and bench results by 2028-03-20 23:59 UTC. (artifact: kvcache_playbook.patch)
2) Autoscaler policy fix and canary (owner: Ben) — patch autoscaler hysteresis and run controlled canary across two dedicated nodes by 2028-03-19 18:00 UTC.
3) Routing policy guardrail (owner: Laura) — add a behavior check to block routing changes that increase avg token window >15% without explicit QA by 2028-03-21 17:00 UTC.
4) Customer-facing RCA doc and exec summary (owner: Sofia) — initial draft by 2028-03-21 12:00 UTC, final by 2028-03-21 17:00 UTC.

Open risks / notes:
- The patch will reduce cache miss amplification but may increase 99th percentile compute slightly during sustained long-prefix traffic; we will test tradeoffs.
- Pelican has a scheduled marketing campaign on 03/22 that will increase peak load; coordination required to validate capacity after fixes.

I've filed the technical ticket referencing this thread: JIRA-9081. Please flag anything missing.

— Karthik
Engineering Manager, Inference Performance, Redwood Inference
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@pelicanretail.com>, Pelican SRE <sre@pelicanretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 17:05:00 +0000
Subject: Final RCA and closure commitments — Pelican Retail throughput regression (03/14)

Alex — thanks again for your patience while we completed verification and testing. Attached is the final RCA and our recommended mitigation schedule (pelican_rca_v1.pdf). High-level takeaway: the incident was caused by an interaction between a routing change that increased model window size and an autoscaler hysteresis setting that delayed scale-up; that combination produced sustained KV cache miss amplification and queuing pressure.

What we delivered:
- Technical patch to KV cache heuristics and bench results (included).
- Autoscaler hysteresis fix deployed to your dedicated pool and validated in canary (see JIRA-9081 for details).
- Routing policy guardrail added to prevent similar unvetted rollouts.

Action items and next steps:
- 2028-03-22 09:00 UTC — joint load validation session with Pelican SRE (owner: Laura Bennett).
- 2028-03-23 15:00 UTC — follow-up exec readout (owner: Sofia Ivanova).
- Weekly verification for 3 weeks post-fix (owner: Ben Carter).

Attachments: pelican_rca_v1.pdf, kvcache_playbook.patch.

If you want an onsite or an extended postmortem readout for Pelican execs, let us know and we will accommodate.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Sr. Technical Account Lead, Redwood Inference
